question: When liquid water (H₂O) cools down to 0 °C (32 °F), it freezes into a solid. What do we call solid water?
explanation: At 0 °C, liquid water (H₂O) freezes into solid ice crystals!
hintText: Think of what you put in a cold drink or skate on in winter!

question: Every magnet has a North (N) pole and a South (S) pole. What happens when you bring a North pole close to a South pole?
optionsString: They pull together (attract)|They push apart (repel)|Nothing happens|They spin in circles
explanation: Opposite magnetic poles (North and South) attract each other, while same poles (N–N or S–S) push apart!
hintText: N and S are opposite poles. Opposite poles act differently from matching poles (N and N).

question: Which planet is the 3rd planet from the Sun and our home with liquid oceans of H₂O?
explanation: Order from the Sun: 1. Mercury, 2. Venus, 3. Earth, 4. Mars. Earth is the 3rd planet!
hintText: Say the planets in order from the Sun and stop at number 3.

question: Plants use sunlight, water (H₂O), and carbon dioxide (CO₂) to make food and release which gas that we breathe?
explanation: During photosynthesis, green plants take in CO₂ and H₂O and release fresh oxygen (O₂) into the air!
hintText: Your body and a burning candle both need this gas from the air.

question: What happens when white sunlight shines through tiny raindrops in the sky?
optionsString: It splits into 7 rainbow colors|It turns pitch black|It freezes into hail|It makes thunder
explanation: Raindrops act like tiny glass prisms, bending white sunlight into the 7 colors of the rainbow!
hintText: Think about what appears in the sky when the sun comes out during a rain shower.

question: How many major planets orbit the Sun in our Solar System (from Mercury out to Neptune)?
explanation: There are 8 major planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.
hintText: Count the rocky planets near the Sun, then the giant planets farther out.

question: Which organ in your chest pumps blood through your entire body all day and night?
explanation: The heart pumps oxygen-rich blood through your arteries and veins.
hintText: It beats steadily: thump-thump, thump-thump.

question: Which part of a plant grows downward into the soil to absorb water and minerals?
explanation: Roots anchor the plant in soil and absorb water and nutrients.
hintText: Think of what holds a big tree firmly in the ground when the wind blows.

question: Which sense organ allows you to hear music and sounds?
explanation: Ears capture sound vibrations in the air and send signals to your brain.
hintText: Think of what you cover when a noise is too loud.

question: Which of these animals is NOCTURNAL (active mainly at night)?
explanation: Owls hunt at night and sleep during the day, making them nocturnal.
hintText: Most of these are busy by day. Which one is awake while you sleep?

question: What falls from clouds as precipitation during cold winter when water freezes?
explanation: When water vapor freezes into ice crystals in cold air, it falls as snow.
hintText: Think of what makes the ground white and fluffy in winter.

question: What happens when you drop an apple from your hand?
optionsString: It floats upward|It falls down toward Earth|It turns sideways|It disappears
explanation: Earth's gravitational force pulls all objects down toward the ground.
hintText: Let go of a toy: which way does it go?

question: What is the process called when liquid puddle water heats up in the sun and turns into invisible vapor in the air?
explanation: Evaporation is the transition of liquid water into invisible gas (water vapor).
hintText: Think of wet washing drying in the sun: the water floats away into the air.

question: How long does it take for Earth to complete ONE full orbit around the Sun?
explanation: Earth takes about 365.25 days (one full year) to orbit the Sun once.
hintText: How long until your birthday comes around again?

question: Animals with backbones (spines) are called vertebrates. Which of these is an INVERTEBRATE (no bones)?
explanation: Jellyfish have soft bodies with no skeleton or backbone (invertebrates).
hintText: Think of which one is soft and wobbly all over, with nothing hard inside.

question: Why do objects cast shadows on the ground on a sunny day?
optionsString: Light goes straight and the object blocks it|The ground absorbs all the sunlight|The object gives off cold darkness|The Sun switches off behind it
explanation: Light rays travel in straight lines. When an opaque object blocks the rays, an unlit shadow forms behind it.
hintText: Hold your hand in front of a lamp: what does your hand do to the light?

question: Which planet is nicknamed the 'Red Planet' because of its rusty iron-rich soil?
explanation: Mars has abundant iron oxide (rust) on its surface, giving it a distinct reddish appearance.
hintText: The 4th planet from the Sun.

question: What do we call animals that eat ONLY plants (like rabbits and cows)?
explanation: Herbivores (from Latin herba = plant) feed exclusively on plant matter.
hintText: Look at the start of each word. One sounds like 'herb', a green plant.

question: Why does the Moon appear to change shape (phases: crescent, half, full) from Earth?
optionsString: The Moon physically grows and shrinks|We see different parts of its sunlit half|Earth's clouds cover parts of the Moon|The Sun turns off one side of the Moon
explanation: As the Moon circles Earth, our viewpoint of the half illuminated by the Sun changes continually.
hintText: Shine a lamp on a ball and walk around it. Does the lit part look the same?

question: What do we call it when an animal blends into its surroundings (like a chameleon or arctic fox)?
explanation: Camouflage allows animals to disguise their appearance to hide from predators or prey.
hintText: Think of playing hide-and-seek in clothes that match the wall.

question: Which of these materials is an ELECTRICAL CONDUCTOR (allows electricity to flow through it)?
explanation: Metals like copper have free electrons and are excellent electrical conductors.
hintText: Think of what a charger cable is made of inside, under its soft cover.

question: What are fossils?
optionsString: Rare rocks formed in space|Remains of ancient life kept in rock|Pieces of fallen meteorites|Frozen water underground
explanation: Fossils are the mineralized remains of ancient plants, animals, or dinosaur bones preserved in stone.
hintText: How scientists study dinosaurs that lived millions of years ago.

question: Which habitat has very little rain, very hot days and cactus plants?
explanation: Deserts get less than 25 cm of rain in a year. Plants like cacti store water so they can live there.
hintText: Think of where a camel feels at home.

question: How is sound created?
optionsString: By very bright light|By very cold air|By something that vibrates|By strong magnets
explanation: Sound is produced when a vibrating object causes pressure waves in the surrounding air, liquid, or solid.
hintText: Put your fingers on your throat and hum. What do you feel?

question: Which invisible force pulls rain, rivers, and all objects down to the ground?
explanation: Gravity is the attractive force that Earth exerts on all masses.
hintText: Jump as high as you can: what brings you back down?

question: How many bones does an adult human body have?
explanation: An adult human skeleton consists of 206 distinct bones.
hintText: Babies have about 300 bones, but many join together as you grow up.
acceptedAnswers: two hundred six|two hundred and six

question: What is the green pigment in plant leaves that absorbs sunlight for photosynthesis?
explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light from the Sun and gives leaves their green color.
hintText: Think of it as the plant's tiny solar panels.

question: Which planet is famous for its massive, beautiful system of rings made of ice and rock particles?
explanation: Saturn is the gas giant renowned for its spectacular, wide ring system.
hintText: Count outward from the Sun: it is the 6th planet.

question: What causes thunder during a thunderstorm?
optionsString: Clouds crashing together like rocks|Lightning heats air so fast that it bursts outward|Rain falling too fast|Wind shaking the mountains
explanation: Lightning heats the surrounding air channel to ~30,000 °C in milliseconds; the rapid explosive expansion creates thunder.
hintText: A popping balloon makes a bang because air moves suddenly.

question: How do bats navigate and find tiny insects in pitch darkness?
optionsString: Echolocation (listening to echoes)|Seeing the heat of insects|Smelling insects from miles away|Following a built-in compass
explanation: Bats use echolocation: high-frequency ultrasound calls bounce off targets and reveal their exact location.
hintText: Shout in a big empty hall or tunnel: what comes back to your ears?

question: What is molten liquid rock called while it is STILL underground inside a volcano?
explanation: Underground it is called magma; once it erupts onto the surface it is called lava.
hintText: Once it pours out into the open air, it gets a new name.

question: What covers approximately 71% of the entire surface of planet Earth?
explanation: Oceans cover roughly 71% of Earth's surface, which is why Earth is called the 'Blue Marble'.
hintText: Spin a globe: which kind of area do you see most?

question: What gas do humans and animals exhale into the air that green plants absorb?
explanation: Animals breathe in O₂ and exhale CO₂; plants use CO₂ in photosynthesis to generate oxygen.
hintText: You breathe this gas out, and fizzy drinks have it in their bubbles.

question: Which animal has feathers?
explanation: Ducks are birds, and all birds have feathers. Feathers keep them warm and dry.
hintText: Feathers belong to birds. Which one is a bird?

question: What does a caterpillar turn into when it is grown up?
explanation: A caterpillar eats and grows, then rests inside a case. It comes out as a butterfly with wings.
hintText: Think of the insect with big colourful wings in the garden.

question: Which of these does a plant need to stay alive?
explanation: Plants drink water through their roots. Without water they dry out and wilt.
hintText: Think of what you pour on a flower pot when the soil is dry.

question: Which sense tells you that a lemon is sour?
explanation: Your tongue has tiny taste buds. They tell you if food is sour, sweet, salty or bitter.
hintText: Which part of your body does the lemon juice touch when you eat it?

question: How often should you brush your teeth?
optionsString: Once a week|Twice a day|Once a month|Only when sore
explanation: Brush in the morning and before bed. That clears away the germs that make holes in teeth.
hintText: Think of the time after you wake up and the time before you go to bed.
acceptedAnswers: 2 times a day|two times a day|morning and evening

question: Why do we wash our hands with soap before eating?
optionsString: To wash off germs|To cool them down|To make them soft|To help nails grow
explanation: Tiny germs sit on your hands, too small to see. Soap and water wash them away, so they do not get into your food.
hintText: Something too small to see sits on your hands and can make you ill.

question: Which material can you see through clearly?
explanation: Glass lets light pass through, so you can see what is behind it. That is why windows are made of glass.
hintText: Think of what a window is made of.

question: Which of these is a liquid?
explanation: Juice flows and can be poured, so it is a liquid. A stone, a spoon and an ice cube are solids.
hintText: A liquid can be poured from one cup into another.

question: In which season do many trees drop their leaves?
explanation: In autumn the days get shorter and cooler. Many trees drop their leaves and rest through the winter.
hintText: The leaves turn yellow, red and brown first.

question: What gives Earth its daylight and warmth?
explanation: The Sun is a huge, very hot ball of glowing gas. Its light and heat reach Earth every day.
hintText: It rises in the morning and sets in the evening.

question: Which of these sounds is the quietest?
explanation: A whisper is very soft, so you must be close to hear it. Drums, horns and thunder are loud.
hintText: Which one do you use to tell a secret?

question: Which object will a magnet pull towards itself?
optionsString: A steel paper clip|A wooden pencil|A rubber band|A glass marble
explanation: Magnets pull things made of iron or steel. Wood, rubber and glass are not pulled by a magnet.
hintText: Look for the object made of metal.

question: A ball is lying still on the grass. You kick it. What does your kick make it do?
explanation: A kick is a push. A push or a pull can make a still thing start to move.
hintText: A kick is a push. What does a push do to a toy car?
acceptedAnswers: it moves|it starts to move|move|roll away

question: Why should you never touch a light switch with wet hands?
optionsString: The light would get dimmer|The switch would get dirty|The water would get hot|You could get an electric shock
explanation: Water lets electricity pass through. With wet hands the electricity could reach your body, so dry your hands first.
hintText: Water and electricity are a dangerous mix.
acceptedAnswers: electric shock|a shock|you get a shock

question: Into which bin should an old newspaper go?
optionsString: Glass bin|Food waste bin|Paper bin|Battery box
explanation: A newspaper is made of paper. Old paper can be turned into new paper and cardboard.
hintText: Think of what a newspaper is made of.

question: Which animal lives in the cold Arctic?
explanation: Polar bears live on the ice of the Arctic. Thick fur and a layer of fat keep them warm.
hintText: Its white fur matches the snow.

question: Which organ do you use to think and remember?
explanation: Your brain sits inside your head. It thinks, remembers and tells your body what to do.
hintText: It is inside your head, kept safe by your skull.

question: What falls from grey clouds as drops of water?
explanation: Clouds are made of tiny drops of water. When the drops grow big and heavy, they fall as rain.
hintText: You need an umbrella for it.

question: Which of these animals lays eggs?
explanation: A hen is a bird, and birds lay eggs. Cows, dogs and mice give birth to live babies.
hintText: Think of where the eggs for breakfast come from.

question: What do we call air that moves?
explanation: Wind is moving air. You cannot see it, but you feel it on your face and see it shake the trees.
hintText: It makes kites fly and leaves dance.

question: Which of these is a living thing?
explanation: A tree is alive: it grows, takes in water and makes seeds. Rocks, clouds and rivers are not alive.
hintText: Living things grow and need food or water.

question: Ice cream left in the sun turns soft and runny. What is this change called?
explanation: Heat turns a solid into a liquid. This is called melting, and it happens to ice, butter and chocolate too.
hintText: The same thing happens to a snowman on a warm day.

question: Which of these animals is a mammal?
explanation: A dolphin breathes air with lungs and feeds its baby with milk, so it is a mammal. A shark is a fish and a penguin is a bird.
hintText: Mammals breathe air and feed their babies with milk.

question: How many legs does an insect, such as an ant or a bee, have?
explanation: Every insect has 6 legs, 3 on each side. Spiders have 8 legs, so they are not insects.
hintText: Picture an ant: count the legs on one side, then double.

question: A tadpole hatches from an egg in a pond. What does it grow into?
explanation: A tadpole has a tail and lives in water. Slowly it grows legs, loses its tail and becomes a frog.
hintText: It grows legs and loses its tail as it gets older.

question: What do fish use to breathe under water?
explanation: Fish have gills on the sides of their head. Gills take the oxygen out of the water.
hintText: Look for the slits on the side of a fish's head.

question: Hedgehogs sleep in a nest of leaves all through the cold winter. What is this long sleep called?
explanation: In winter there is little food. Hedgehogs save energy by sleeping for months. This is called hibernation.
hintText: It is a way to save energy when food is hard to find in winter.

question: Which part of a plant makes the seeds?
explanation: Seeds form inside the flower. Later the flower turns into a fruit with the seeds in it.
hintText: It is the colourful part that bees like to visit.

question: How do the fluffy seeds of a dandelion travel to new places?
optionsString: By water|On animal fur|By wind|Inside birds
explanation: Each dandelion seed has a tiny fluffy parachute. The wind lifts it and carries it far away.
hintText: What happens when you blow on a dandelion clock?

question: Which body parts pull on your bones to make you move?
explanation: Muscles are joined to your bones. When a muscle gets shorter, it pulls the bone and your arm or leg moves.
hintText: Bend your arm and feel what gets hard and thick above your elbow.

question: Which organ mixes and breaks down the food you swallow?
explanation: Food slides down a tube into your stomach. There it is mixed with juices and broken into tiny bits.
hintText: It rumbles when you are hungry.

question: About how long should a child of your age sleep each night?
explanation: School children need about 9 to 11 hours of sleep. While you sleep, your body grows and your brain sorts what you learned.
hintText: Count from an early bedtime to the time you get up for school.

question: Is the air around us a solid, a liquid or a gas?
optionsString: A gas|A liquid|A solid|Nothing at all
explanation: Air is a mix of gases. You cannot see it, but it fills a balloon and you feel it as wind.
hintText: It spreads out to fill any space, like the inside of a balloon.

question: You pour juice from a tall glass into a wide bowl. What happens to the juice?
optionsString: It turns into a gas|It keeps its tall shape|It gets heavier|It takes the bowl's shape
explanation: A liquid has no shape of its own. It always takes the shape of the cup or bowl that holds it.
hintText: Think about how water looks in a bottle, a cup and a puddle.

question: What are clouds made of?
optionsString: Smoke from fires|Tiny drops of water|Fine white dust|Thick warm air
explanation: Warm, wet air rises and cools. The water in it turns into tiny drops, and millions of them make a cloud.
hintText: Think of the mist you see when you breathe out on a cold day.

question: Which tool measures how warm or cold the air is?
explanation: A thermometer shows the temperature in degrees. A high number means warm, a low number means cold.
hintText: A doctor uses a small one to check if you have a fever.

question: Why do we have day and night?
optionsString: The Sun circles Earth|The Moon hides the Sun|Earth spins like a top|Clouds cover the Sun
explanation: Earth spins around once every 24 hours. The side facing the Sun has day, and the other side has night.
hintText: Shine a torch on a ball and slowly turn the ball.
acceptedAnswers: Earth spins|the Earth spins|Earth turns|Earth rotates

question: In which direction does the Sun rise in the morning?
explanation: Earth spins towards the east, so we see the Sun come up in the east. In the evening it sets in the west.
hintText: It is the opposite of where the Sun sets in the evening.

question: What is the Sun?
explanation: The Sun is a star, a giant ball of glowing hot gas. It looks bigger than other stars because it is much closer to us.
hintText: It makes its own light, like the tiny lights in the night sky.

question: You shout in a mountain valley and hear your voice come back. What is this called?
explanation: Sound bounces off hard walls like rock. The sound that comes back to your ears is an echo.
hintText: Sound can bounce off a hard wall, like a ball.

question: On which floor will a toy car roll the farthest after the same push?
explanation: A smooth floor rubs against the wheels only a little. Rough carpet, grass and sand rub more and slow the car sooner.
hintText: Rough ground rubs against the wheels and slows them down.

question: A battery, wires and a bulb make a loop, and the bulb glows. What happens if one wire comes loose?
optionsString: The bulb gets brighter|The bulb starts to blink|The battery fills up|The bulb goes out
explanation: Electricity flows only around a complete loop. A loose wire breaks the loop, so the bulb goes out.
hintText: Electricity needs an unbroken path all the way around.
acceptedAnswers: it goes out|the light goes out|it turns off

question: Fruit peels and old leaves rot in a compost heap. What do they turn into?
explanation: Worms and tiny living things eat the peels and leaves. They turn them into dark, rich soil that feeds new plants.
hintText: Gardeners spread it on their beds to help plants grow.

question: Which of these small animals is NOT an insect?
explanation: Insects have 6 legs. A spider has 8 legs and no wings, so it belongs to a different group.
hintText: Count the legs: an insect always has six.

question: A frog starts life in water and later lives on land too. Which animal group is it in?
explanation: Amphibians such as frogs and newts begin life in water and later breathe air on land. Their skin is soft and moist.
hintText: Its skin is soft and wet, not dry and scaly like a lizard's.

question: A butterfly's life has four stages. Which stage comes right after the caterpillar?
explanation: The order is egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly. Inside the chrysalis the caterpillar slowly changes into a butterfly.
hintText: The caterpillar hangs still inside a hard case before it gets wings.

question: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower so that seeds can form. What is this called?
explanation: Pollen is a fine yellow powder made by flowers. When it reaches another flower, that flower can make seeds. This is pollination.
hintText: Without this step an apple tree would grow no apples.

question: What does almost every food chain start with?
optionsString: A meat eater|A plant eater|A green plant|A small insect
explanation: Green plants make their own food from sunlight. Animals cannot do this, so a food chain begins with a plant, such as grass → rabbit → fox.
hintText: Who can make food from sunlight without eating anything?

question: What is stored inside a camel's hump?
explanation: The hump is a store of fat. The camel uses this fat as food when it finds nothing to eat in the desert. It is not a water tank.
hintText: The hump gets smaller when the camel has had nothing to eat for a long time.

question: Swallows fly to warm lands every autumn and come back in spring. What is this journey called?
explanation: In winter swallows find no insects to eat here. So they fly far south and return in spring. This yearly journey is called migration.
hintText: It is a long trip that the birds repeat every single year.

question: What carries messages between your brain and the rest of your body?
explanation: Nerves are like thin wires that run through your whole body. They carry signals to and from your brain very fast.
hintText: They work like tiny telephone wires inside you.

question: Milk and cheese give your body calcium. What does your body need calcium for most of all?
optionsString: For shiny hair|For sharp eyes|For strong bones|For soft skin
explanation: Calcium makes bones and teeth hard. Milk, cheese and yoghurt give you plenty of it while you grow.
hintText: Think of the hardest parts inside your body.
acceptedAnswers: bones|strong bones|bones and teeth|strong bones and teeth|teeth

question: Which of these changes can NOT be undone?
optionsString: Frying an egg|Melting ice|Freezing juice|Melting chocolate
explanation: Ice, juice and chocolate can be frozen and melted again and again. A fried egg can never become a raw egg again.
hintText: Ask for each one: can I get the first thing back by cooling or warming it?

question: You stir a spoon of sugar into warm water and it seems to vanish. What happened to the sugar?
explanation: The sugar broke into bits too small to see and spread through the water. It is still there: the water tastes sweet. This is called dissolving.
hintText: Taste the water: the sugar is still in there, mixed in.

question: On a xylophone, which bars make the highest notes?
optionsString: The longest bars|The widest bars|The middle bars|The shortest bars
explanation: A short bar shakes back and forth very quickly, and fast shaking makes a high note. Long bars shake slowly and sound low.
hintText: Small things usually shake faster than big things.

question: On a cold day, tiny drops of water form on the inside of a window. What is this called?
explanation: Warm air in the room holds invisible water vapour. When it touches the cold glass, it cools and turns back into drops of water. This is condensation.
hintText: It is the opposite of a puddle drying up in the sun.

question: What kind of water is most of the water on Earth?
optionsString: Salty sea water|Fresh river water|Rain water|Water in lakes
explanation: Almost all of Earth's water is in the salty seas and oceans. Only a small part is fresh water that we can drink.
hintText: Look at a globe and find where the biggest blue areas are.

question: What is fog?
optionsString: Smoke from chimneys|Very fine snow|Dust in the wind|A cloud near the ground
explanation: Fog is made of tiny drops of water floating in the air, just like a cloud. The only difference is that it touches the ground.
hintText: Think of what you would walk through on top of a very high mountain.
acceptedAnswers: a cloud|a low cloud|cloud on the ground

question: Why do you see lightning before you hear its thunder?
optionsString: Thunder starts later|Light is faster than sound|Sound is faster than light|Clouds slow the sound
explanation: Lightning and thunder happen at the same moment. Light reaches you almost at once, but sound travels much more slowly, so the thunder arrives later.
hintText: Both start together, but they travel to you at different speeds.
acceptedAnswers: light travels faster than sound|light is faster

question: About how long does the Moon take to travel once around Earth?
explanation: The Moon needs about 27 days to circle Earth, which is close to one month. The word 'month' even comes from 'Moon'.
hintText: Count the days from one full Moon to the next.
acceptedAnswers: 1 month|one month|a month|about a month|27 days

question: Which planet is the closest to the Sun?
explanation: Mercury is the first planet from the Sun. Then come Venus, Earth and Mars.
hintText: It races around the Sun faster than any other planet.

question: The Moon does not make its own light. Why does it shine at night?
optionsString: It glows from heat inside|It burns like a candle|Stars light it up|It reflects sunlight
explanation: The Moon is a ball of rock. Sunlight falls on it and bounces off towards Earth, like light from a mirror.
hintText: Think of how a white wall looks bright when a torch shines on it.
acceptedAnswers: it reflects the Sun's light|sunlight bounces off it|reflects sunlight

question: At what time on a sunny day is your shadow the shortest?
optionsString: At sunrise|At midday|In late afternoon|At sunset
explanation: At midday the Sun is at its highest point in the sky. Light then comes from high above, so your shadow is short.
hintText: A lamp held high above a toy makes a small shadow. When is the Sun highest?

question: You move your hand closer to a lamp. What happens to its shadow on the wall?
optionsString: It gets smaller|It disappears|It gets bigger|It stays the same
explanation: Near the lamp your hand blocks more of the light that spreads out from it. So the shadow on the wall grows.
hintText: Close to the lamp, your hand stands in the way of more light.

question: A parachute falls slowly and gently. What pushes up against it and slows it down?
explanation: The wide parachute has to push a lot of air out of its way. The air pushes back and slows the fall. This push is called air resistance.
hintText: Run with a big open umbrella: what do you feel pushing against it?

question: Not every metal sticks to a magnet. Which of these metals does a magnet attract?
explanation: Magnets attract iron and things that contain iron, such as steel. Aluminium, copper and gold are metals too, but a magnet does not pull them.
hintText: Steel nails and paper clips are made mostly of this metal.

question: Why is the metal wire in a cable covered with plastic?
optionsString: To make the wire stronger|To keep the wire warm|To keep the electricity in|To make the cable lighter
explanation: Electricity flows easily through metal but not through plastic. The plastic cover keeps the electricity inside the wire, so you can touch the cable safely.
hintText: Electricity can pass through metal, but not through this cover.
